sentences.text:
The Honourable Smt. Justice K.Sujana
 Criminal Petition No.1280 Of 2024
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner, who is accused No.1 in CC No.371 of 2023, under Section 482 Cr.PC to quash the proceedings in CC No.371 of 2023 for the offences under Sections 324, 504 read with 34 IPC.
2.

The facts of the case are that on 25.05.2023, the de facto complainant gave complaint stating that when he along with his friend went to pan shop at Borabanda to eat pan and some persons were present near the pan shop and among them petitioner/accused No.1 gave birthday party, wherein the accused No.1 saw the de facto complainant and picked up quarrel with him by abusing him in filthy language and caught hold of his shirt collar and gave fist blows on his face due to which he sustained injuries in the left ear and then his friend Mahesh tried to rescue the petitioner but the accused No.1 Narsmimhulu, Narendra and others beat the de facto complainant and his friends.
Stating so, he requested to take necessary action.

As such, the police registered a case under Sections 324 and 504 read with 34 IPC.
3.
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that as per the averments made in the complaint there was no usage of dangerous weapons with an intention to cause voluntary hurt.

The foremost ingredient of committing an offence under Section 504 IPC is an intentional insult and that it was intended to provoke a person into breaking the peace, but in the present case, as per the averments in the complaint, there was no such intention to insult the defacto-complainant.
There are lot of discrepancies between the complaint, charge sheet and Section 164 statements which manifestly and categorically shows that the contents of the complainant are false and frivolous.

There are two different dates in the charge sheet and this is only a false case which is foisted against the petitioner and even if the averments in the complainant taken on their face do not constitute the ingredients necessary for the offence by petitioner under Sections 324, 504 r/w 34 IPC.

As such,
prayed the Court to quash the proceedings.
4. Heard Mr. Kullapareddy Suresh Babu learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though this petitioner is shown as accused for the offences under Sections 324, 504 r/w 34 IPC, the complainant ingredients does not constitute either of the offences and further there are discrepancies in the statement held in the chargesheet.
It is also further submitted that there is no dangerous weapon used in the commission of the offence.
Therefore, offence under Section 324 IPC does not attract and there is no intentional insult as per the averments of the complaint or the statements.
As such prayed this Court to quash the proceedings.

sentences.text: 6. Though notice served on the respondent, none appeared on behalf of the respondent.

7. The learned Public Prosecutor would submit that it is not a stage to see that discrepancies in the complaint and statements, as a stone was recovered by the police and the same is sufficient to constitute the offences under Section 324 IPC.
Further, the petitioner/Accused used abusive language.
Therefore, Section 504 IPC also constitutes against the petitioner.
At this stage, there are no grounds to quash the proceedings.
As such prayed this Court to dismiss the petition.

8. Having regard to the rival submissions and also the material available on record, it is to be noted that to quash the proceedings the petitioner has to prove that the averments in the complaint and the statements even if they are taken in entirety, they does not constitute any offence, whereas, in the present case it is clearly mentioned that this petitioner beat the de facto complainant with a stone and also abused him.

The petitioner counsel submitted that there are discrepancies and contradictions in the statement which does not constitute any offence whereas, in the Judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1Hazrat Deen vs. State of Uttar Pradesh in Para Nos.5 and 6 it was observed as under:
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has not been charged only under the POCSO Act.

Even assuming that the petitioner could not have been charged under the POCSO Act, the petitioner has been charged under various provisions of the IPC which were admittedly in force on the date of the alleged offence.
The learned counsel for the petitioner emphatically argued that the FIR does not disclose offence under Section 376 of the IPC.
The FIR is the initial document.

In her statement given by the prosecutrix under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) after the prosecutrix attained majority, she categorically made statements which tantamount to offence under Section 376 of the IPC.
2022 SCC Online SC 1781 6.
Discrepancies between the FIR and any subsequent statement under Section 164 of the CrPC may be a defence.
However, the discrepancies cannot be a ground for discharge without initiation of trial."
9. In view thereof, it is not safe to quash the proceedings against accused No.1 and the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is dismissed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
